q1_issues.issue: "his son's death" is given the class `die`, but `death` -> `die` is derivation across parts of speech, which the instruction set bars (lemmatize by inflection only); the event-denoting noun should keep its own form.

`(Patient sk_die_1 sk_boy_1)` is a role atom asserted at top level for a referent introduced only inside the sealed complement, where the instruction set projects the `Member`/`Name` typing atom alone.

"wants ... to be held responsible" is a control verb with a to-infinitive, which the instruction set says never seals; the complement event should be reified as sibling atoms and attached by `(Theme sk_want_1 sk_hold_1)`, not nested as an `(And ...)` term.

"everyone" is an explicit universal, which the instruction set distributes through an `Implication` rule over `(Member $x person)`; the parse substitutes a group witness `sk_people_1` and predicates over it as a unit.

`(Member sk_people_1 responsible)` predicates a member-level property of the group symbol, the exact reading the plural rules forbid (a bare `(Member <group> <prop>)` is only for a property of the collection itself).
the reified "involved in ..." adjective state omits the mandatory dual-emit flat copular atom that the adjective-PP-complement rule requires alongside the state witness.
the appositive age "33" is emitted bare, but an appositive takes the host clause's wrapper and the host ("said") is past, so a `Past` wrapper is expected as on any tensed measure.

q2_gaps: "hold NP + predicative adjective" ("held responsible") — an attitude/judgement ascription; neither the resultative shape (which requires the object to change) nor the impersonal-reported-attitude template squarely covers it
a universal quantifier ("everyone") inside a sealed complement — the universal's prescribed `Implication` rule form has no defined placement inside a seal
a possessive genitive on a deverbal nominalization naming its undergoer ("his son's death") — the complements section covers only the of-phrase object case
notes: The source text is garbled ("They boy's" for "The boy's"); the parse reasonably reads it as the definite possessive. Doubly-embedded seals (say > want > hold) are where most of the divergence sits.
